openers.title: The Bulging Sunlit Bottle
openers.question: A half-empty sealed water bottle left in a hot parked car swells taut, while a pressure sensor detects a sharp spike in overhead gas. What are the surface water particles doing in response to rising temperature that forces so many more molecules into the vapor space?
openers.model_answer: Higher thermal energy shifts the kinetic energy distribution so an exponentially larger fraction of liquid molecules possess sufficient energy to overcome intermolecular attractions and vaporize.
openers.target: Clausius-Clapeyron exponential increase of vapor pressure with temperature

openers.title: The Boiling Bell Jar Flash
openers.question: Unheated lukewarm water inside a vacuum chamber suddenly bubbles and boils furiously, tracked by a headspace pressure sensor. What are the energetic water particles doing at the liquid boundary that enables them to lift into vapor without any added heat?
openers.model_answer: Vapor pressure equals the lowered external atmospheric pressure, allowing molecules throughout the liquid to overcome the containment barrier and nucleate vapor bubbles.
openers.target: Boiling point definition as vapor pressure equaling atmospheric pressure

openers.title: The Rubbing Alcohol Chill
openers.question: Dabbing rubbing alcohol onto skin produces intense cold and rapid drying compared to water, while a vapor monitor logs a towering rate of escaping gas. What are the liquid alcohol molecules doing compared to water molecules that lets them flee into vapor so eagerly?
openers.model_answer: Alcohol molecules have weaker intermolecular attractions than water, so a larger fraction of particles can overcome cohesive forces at room temperature to evaporate.
openers.target: Intermolecular force strength dictating relative vapor pressure and volatility

openers.title: The Crushed Cooled Flask
openers.question: Sealing steam inside a rigid glass jug and plunging it into cold water causes the walls to implode, recorded by an internal barometer. What are the bouncing vapor particles doing against the cold glass surfaces that collapses overhead pressure so violently?
openers.model_answer: Cooling reduces molecular kinetic energy, causing vapor molecules colliding with cold walls to lose energy, condense into liquid, and deplete the vapor phase.
openers.target: Dynamic condensation and vapor pressure collapse upon cooling

openers.title: The Ten-Degree Vapor Surge
openers.question: Warming perfume water ten degrees doubles the overhead vapor reading on a volatile sensor, far surpassing the minor jump in thermal motion. What are the liquid molecules doing internally to yield such a disproportionately massive surge of vapor from a modest temperature bump?
openers.model_answer: The Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution causes the proportion of particles with energy exceeding the enthalpy of vaporization to grow exponentially rather than linearly with temperature.
openers.target: Non-linear Maxwell-Boltzmann tail growth driving Clausius-Clapeyron behavior

openers.title: The Sealed Syringe Standoff
openers.question: Pulling back the plunger of a sealed syringe containing liquid water momentarily drops pressure before an electronic gauge shows it climbing right back to its original value. What are the surface liquid particles doing in the expanded chamber to restore the exact starting pressure?
openers.model_answer: Molecules evaporate faster than vapor condenses until dynamic equilibrium is re-established, restoring the equilibrium vapor pressure characteristic of that specific temperature.
openers.target: Equilibrium vapor pressure as an intensive, volume-independent property at constant temperature
